## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) with \(t>r+s-n\), \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) is the unique nonidentity bigrassmannian in \(S_n\) with \(\Des(v)=\{(r\leftrightarrow r+1)\}\), \(\Des(v^{-1})=\{(s\leftrightarrow s+1)\}\), \(v_t=s+1\), explicitly
  \[
  (1,\ldots,t-1,\ s+1,\ldots,s+r-t+1,\ t,\ldots,s,\ s+r-t+2,\ldots,n).
  \]
  [source-2, lines 973-993]
- [source-backed] \(J_v:=\Bbbk\text{-span}\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\); in the type-\(A\) integral setting, \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is treated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\). [source-2, lines 334-348; source-2, lines 1344-1350; source-2, lines 1369-1375]
- [source-backed] The \(r\)-grassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) corresponds to the rectangle \(i^j\), where \(i=s-t+1\) and \(j=r-t+1\). [source-2, lines 1354-1362]
- [source-backed] With \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), set \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). Theorem 5.4 states that \(J_v\) is generated by either
  \[
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}
  \quad\text{or}\quad
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}.
  \]
  [source-2, lines 1380-1402]
- [source-backed] The formal conjecture is: “The two generating sets for the ideal \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) given in Theorem 5.4 are both minimal.” The authors report computer verification for all bigrassmannian permutations with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2, lines 1489-1502]
- [source-backed] Taking \(M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), the source conjectures that \(M/\Lambda_+M\) requires \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators and suspects the stronger isomorphism
  \[
  J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}/\Lambda_+J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}.
  \]
  [source-2, lines 1536-1552]
- [source-backed] The related, formally posed type-\(A_{n-1}\) open question asks for a minimal generating set of \(I_w\), including for varieties defined by inclusions (avoiding \(4231,35142,42513,351624\)) and smooth varieties (avoiding \(3412,4231\)). [source-2, lines 1913-1929]

## Strategy
Use the two Theorem 5.4 intervals as the candidate generating families; minimality concerns inclusion-minimal generation of \(J_v\), while the quotient statement is a stronger, separately prose-stated assertion.

## Gaps
- \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}(x_1,x_2,\ldots)\) is defined in the supplied excerpt, but \(\Lambda_+\) is not explicitly defined there; it occurs in the proposition and quotient formulation. [source-2, lines 1310-1323; source-2, lines 1517-1552]
- The source says the quotient is a finitely generated abelian group but does not, in supplied lines, define \(\Lambda_+\) as a particular graded ideal. [source-2, lines 1536-1552]
- The phrase “we say \(u\) is \(r\)-grassmannian” follows a condition on \(w\), an apparent variable-name typo not affecting the stated \(v\)-formulas. [source-2, lines 1294-1307]

## Next
Establish or test minimality through the images of the displayed Schur generators in \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), keeping the quotient-isomorphism statement distinct from the formal conjecture.
